proposals.label: Argue That Existing Laws Already Govern AI, Requiring No New AI-Specific Statutes
proposals.description: An Intention within accelerationist discourse that asserts AI is not legally exceptional — that existing, technology-neutral bodies of law (contract, tort, product liability, consumer protection, antidiscrimination, intellectual property, and sector-specific rules) already reach AI's harms and capabilities, so bespoke AI-specific legislation is unnecessary and would chiefly serve to slow deployment. Proponents use this to resist new regulatory regimes by placing the burden of proof on those who claim a genuine legal gap, and by framing AI as a general-purpose tool to be governed by how it is used rather than by the technology itself. Encompasses: applying existing statutes and common-law doctrines to AI harms, 'same activity, same rules' technology-neutrality arguments, characterizing proposed AI-specific law as redundant with existing coverage, and demanding demonstration of a concrete legal gap before any new statute. Excludes: the opposing pole that AI requires entirely new legal frameworks (acc-intentions-047); the design of new use-case- or domain-calibrated AI regulation (skp-intentions-007, skp-intentions-139), which still authors AI-tailored rules rather than relying on inherited law; and the generic claim that precaution stifles progress absent the specific existing-law-suffices argument (acc-intentions-056, the intended parent intention).
proposals.rationale: The taxonomy has the 'new laws' pole (acc-intentions-047) but no positive counterpart for the anti-exceptionalism / adapt-existing-law intention (confirmed by search across acc/saf/skp — the nearest neighbors skp-intentions-007 and skp-139 are skeptic-camp use-case/domain-calibrated *new* regulation, not the accelerationist existing-law-suffices pole). This gap forces anti-exceptionalism sources to land as opposed on acc-intentions-047. Intended parent: acc-intentions-056 ('Discredit Precautionary AI Regulation as Progress-Blocking'), as a sibling of acc-intentions-047 making the new-laws vs existing-law poles explicit.
